name: Dry brush
lead: Dry brushing is the practice of stroking a stiff natural-bristle brush over dry skin, usually before a shower and moving toward the heart. It draws on Ayurvedic practice and is promoted for smoother skin, better circulation and lymph drainage.
Its looksmaxxing use is as a cheap exfoliant. The entry's rating is limited because physical exfoliation is plausible while the lymphatic, detox and cellulite claims have no good clinical support.

paras: The bristles abrade dead surface cells and briefly increase blood flow to the skin, giving a pink, smoother look. There is no good evidence that it moves lymph in healthy people; clinical manual lymphatic drainage is a separate, trained technique.

Brushing is generally safe on intact skin if gentle, but should be avoided on rashes, eczema, psoriasis, sunburn, wounds or active acne. Over-brushing damages the barrier. Brushes need regular cleaning. Claims about detoxification and cellulite removal are marketing; the secondary sources reviewed here found no rigorous trials.
